newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian union in dispute with Entergy.
newsitem.headline: Australian union in dispute with Entergy.

text.p: Striking Australian power workers said on Tuesday said U.S-based Entergy Corp needs to abandon its industrial relations "warfare" if it hoped to expand in Australia.

The Victoria state branch of the Electrical Trades Union of Australia (ETU) said it briefed the state government of New South Wales (NSW) on its dispute with Victorian electricity distributor, CitiPower, a unit of Entergy.
The NSW Labor Party government has flagged the possibile privatisation of the state's power industry which could raise up to A$22 billion and pay off the state's debt.
CitiPower, one of Victoria's five privatised power companies, has been locked in an eight week strike of 140 workers after pay negotiations broke down in May.
Entergy acquired CitiPower in February 1996 for A$1.75 billion out of a total of A$9 billion raised by the conservative Victorian state government in the sale of the five power distributors.

NSW Treasurer Michael Egan said the dispute was unfortunate for all concerned and said the if the government won approval to sell the state's power assets it would seek investors with a "good record on industrial relations."
The proposal requires the approval of the NSW state cabinet and faces opposition from the left of the Labor Party which is committed to public ownership.
CitiPower spokesman Ross Gilmore told Reuters the dispute in Victoria had nothing to do with any potential involvement by Entergy in the NSW power industry.
